page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 server family. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization with dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. A local storage disk of 1890 GB is bundled with the instance, and it supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in memory bandwidth and integer operations. Uncached large-block memory read and write speeds reach 211.12 GB/sec and 102.72 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores also demonstrate strong performance. Image processing is a notable highlight, scoring in the top 10% tier. For language model workloads, the server delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 396.8 tokens/sec on small 135M models, though performance drops to a weak 2.77 tokens/sec for text generation on large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32lds_v6 offers a resource-dense compute profile with a lower memory-to-CPU ratio, making it a viable option for workloads that require high raw processing power and local storage without the overhead of excess RAM. The inclusion of a 1890 GB local disk provides high-speed temporary storage. This configuration is well-suited for compute-heavy tasks, image processing, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.

It features 16 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 1890 GB local disk. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V with dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is optimized for compute-heavy workloads. Benchmark results show strong performance in large-block memory bandwidth, multi-threaded decompression, and single-core processing, alongside top-tier image processing and small-model LLM text generation. However, its 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a low-memory tradeoff, and text generation performance on large 70B models is weak. This server is best suited for static web serving, image processing, and compute-intensive applications requiring local storage.
